primary_task: Create a PDF document with reportlab and verify its layout by rendering the pages to PNG with pdftoppm and inspecting them before delivery.

requirements.name: reportlab
requirements.evidence: 2. Use `reportlab` to generate PDFs when creating new documents.
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads)"

requirements.name: pdftoppm (poppler-utils)
requirements.evidence: Do not deliver until the latest PNG inspection shows zero visual or formatting defects. ... sudo apt-get install -y poppler-utils ... pdftoppm -png $INPUT_PDF $OUTPUT_PREFIX
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, ...)"; egress_allow lists "archive.ubuntu.com"

requirements.name: pdfplumber or pypdf
requirements.evidence: 3. Use `pdfplumber` (or `pypdf`) for text extraction and quick checks
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)"

requirements.name: uv or pip
requirements.evidence: uv pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf ... If `uv` is unavailable: python3 -m pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)" (pip is the alternative to uv; uv itself is on PyPI)

requirements.name: read (image inspection)
requirements.evidence: 1. Prefer visual review: render PDF pages to PNGs and inspect them.
requirements.basis: tools.read: "read files in the working directory"

notes: Took creating a PDF as the representative request. The macOS brew path is an alternative and not needed on Linux. The read tool's ability to view PNG images is assumed from "read files"; the manifest does not say it renders images (unknown in that strict sense, but the document also allows asking the user to review locally). If the request is only to read a PDF, pdfplumber/pypdf become the hard requirement; still installable.
